q: Chapter 7 of GFR 2017 (Inventory Management) spans which rules?
e: Chapter 7 = Inventory Management, Rules 207 to 223 (17 rules). Chapter 6 is procurement (142–206) and Chapter 8 is contract management (224–227A).

q: Fixed assets should be physically verified —
a: only at the time of audit
e: Rule 213(1): fixed assets should be verified at least once in a year, the inventory is ordinarily maintained at site, and the outcome is recorded in the corresponding register.

q: Physical verification of consumable goods and materials must be done —
a: only when a new officer takes charge
e: Rule 213(2): a physical verification of all consumable goods and materials should be undertaken at least once in a year.

q: A library holds 30,000 volumes. Complete physical verification should be done —
a: at least once in three years
e: Rule 215(i): ≤20,000 volumes → every year; more than 20,000 and up to 50,000 → at least once in three years; more than 50,000 → sample verification at intervals of not more than three years.

q: Library with more than 50,000 volumes — the rule requires —
a: sample physical verification at intervals of not more than 3 years
e: Rule 215(i): for libraries having more than 50,000 volumes, sample physical verification at intervals of not more than three years. If it reveals unusual/unreasonable shortages, complete verification is done.

q: Loss of how many volumes per 1,000 volumes issued/consulted in a year may be taken as reasonable?
e: Rule 215(ii): loss of five volumes per one thousand volumes issued/consulted in a year is reasonable — provided it is not attributable to dishonesty or negligence. A book valued above ₹1,000, and rare books, must always be investigated.

q: A material remaining in stock for over ___ shall generally be considered surplus.
e: Rule 214 note: a material remaining in stock for over a year shall generally be considered surplus unless adequate reasons to treat it otherwise exist — it is rebuttable, not automatic.

q: Current threshold: surplus/obsolete goods of assessed residual value above ____ must go by advertised tender or public auction.
e: Rule 218(i): above ₹4,00,000. This was enhanced from ₹2,00,000 by DoE OM No. F.1/3/2024-PPD dated 10.07.2024.

q: Bid security in disposal through advertised tender is ordinarily —
e: Rule 219: bid security shall ordinarily be 10% of the assessed or reserved price, and the amount must be stated in the bidding document.

q: On acceptance of a bid at auction, earnest money to be taken on the spot is —
a: not less than 10% of bid value
not less than 25% of bid value
not less than 50% of bid value
e: Rule 220: earnest money of not less than 25% of the bid value, immediately on the spot, in cash or by Deposit-at-Call-Receipt (DACR).

q: The auction team must compulsorily include —
a: an officer of the Internal Finance Wing
e: Rule 220: the composition of the auction team is decided by the competent authority, but it must include an officer of the Internal Finance Wing of the department.

q: Expired medicines, food grain and ammunition should be —
a: disposed of or destroyed immediately by a suitable mode
stored for three years, then sold
e: Rule 218(iii): such hazardous or unfit-for-human-consumption goods shall be disposed of or destroyed immediately, to avoid health hazard, environmental pollution and misuse.

q: Hire charges for a fixed asset hired out to a contractor are calculated on the basis of —
e: Rule 212: calculation of charges recoverable from local bodies, contractors and others shall be based on the historical cost.

q: Sale at scrap value is permitted —
a: after tender and auction attempts fail, with competent authority approval in consultation with the Finance division
only with Ministry of Finance approval in every case
e: Rule 221: only after attempts through advertised tender or auction fail, and with competent authority approval in consultation with the Finance division.

q: Under Rule 223, formal sanction of the competent authority for a loss is required —
a: only if the loss exceeds ₹1 lakh
only when the accounts are actually adjusted
even though no formal correction or adjustment in Government accounts is involved
e: Rule 223(1) uses the exact phrase “even though no formal correction or adjustment in Government accounts is involved”. This is a classic exam trap.

q: How many heads are prescribed for losses NOT due to depreciation?
e: Rule 223(3): five heads — theft or fraud; neglect; anticipated losses on obsolescence/excess purchases; damage; and Force Majeure (fire, flood, enemy action). Losses due to depreciation have four heads.

q: On transfer of the Officer-in-charge of stores, the handing-over statement is signed by —
a: both the relieving and the relieved officer, with date, each retaining a copy
e: Rule 216: the statement with all relevant details is prepared and signed with date by both the relieving and relieved officer, and each retains a copy.

q: The report of stores for disposal is prepared in —
e: Rule 217(iii): report of stores for disposal → Form GFR-10. The sale account after disposal → Form GFR-11 (Rule 222).

q: Under Rule 208(1)(ii), which inspection is mandatory on every receipt from a private supplier?
e: Rule 208(1)(ii): sab materials ko counted/measured/weighed karne ke saath visual inspection zaroori hai. Technical inspection "where required" hai.

q: Rule 209(iv) deals with —
a: Partial compliance of an indent and alternative materials
e: Rule 209(iv): agar poora indent pura na ho sake to jitna uplabdh hai utna supply karein aur indentor ki copy mein entry karein; alternative material ho to document mein zikr kiya ja sakta hai.

q: The Note under Rule 211 permits Ministries/Departments to —
a: Supplement the prescribed forms with additional details
Replace GFR-23 with any private format
e: Note: "These forms can be supplemented with additional details by Ministries/Departments as required." Supplement karna hai, replace karna nahi.

q: Rule 213(3)(iii) routes discrepancies identified during verification to —
e: Rule 213(3)(iii) specifically says action "in accordance with provision given in Rule 33 to 38" — Chapter 2 ka loss-reporting framework.

q: A rare book goes missing from a government library. Under Rule 215(ii) —
a: It is covered by the 5 per 1,000 concession
It must invariably be investigated, irrespective of value
No action is needed if the library has over 50,000 volumes
It can be written off by the librarian
e: Rule 215(ii): rare books irrespective of value aur ₹1,000 se upar ki kitaab — dono ki loss ki investigation invariably hogi.

q: Under Rule 217(iii), when the book value cannot be worked out, —
a: The item cannot be disposed of
The original purchase price may be utilised
The reserved price is deemed nil
Ministry of Finance approval is mandatory in every case
e: Rule 217(iii) khud fallback deta hai: "the original purchase price of the goods in question may be utilised".

q: How many "broad steps" are listed in Rule 219(i)?
e: Rule 219(i) mein nau steps hain (a) se (i) — aakhri step unsuccessful bidders ki bid security return karna hai.

q: If the highest acceptable responsive bidder cannot lift the entire quantity, the balance may be offered to the next bidder(s) —
a: At the price offered by the highest acceptable bidder
Only after Ministry of Finance approval
e: Rule 219(ii)(e): remaining quantity next higher bidder(s) ko usi price par offer ki ja sakti hai jo highest acceptable bidder ne offer kiya tha.

q: Earnest money at the fall of the hammer must be —
a: Not less than 10% of bid value, within 7 days
Not less than 25% of bid value, immediately on the spot
The full bid value within 24 hours
At the discretion of the auctioneer
e: Rule 220(iv): not less than 25% of bid value, immediately on the spot, cash ya DACR (Ministry/Department ke favour mein).

q: Which two conditions must be satisfied before selling at scrap value?
a: Prior failure of advertised tender/auction attempts; then competent authority approval in consultation with Finance division
Ministry of Finance approval and re-tender
e: Rule 221: pehle tender+auction dono try karne honge, phir competent authority approval in consultation with Finance division.

q: The sale account under Rule 222 must be signed by —
a: The officer who supervised the sale or auction
e: Rule 222: Form GFR-11, "duly signed by the officer who supervised the sale or auction".

q: Which of these is NOT one of the four heads for losses due to depreciation?
a: Losses due to theft or fraud
e: Theft/fraud Rule 223(3)(i) mein aata hai — non-depreciation wala head. Depreciation ke 4 heads hain: market fluctuation, wear & tear, lack of foresight in purchases, negligence after purchase.

q: Rule 218(iii) covers expired medicines, food grain and ammunition. The rule requires —
a: Sale by advertised tender above ₹4 lakh
Immediate disposal or destruction by a suitable mode
Storage for three years before disposal
e: Rule 218(iii): hazardous ya human consumption ke layak na hone wale items ko turant dispose/destroy karein — health hazard, pollution aur misuse se bachne ke liye. Threshold in par lagta nahi.

q: Security-sensitive items such as currency, stamps, receipt books and security press must be disposed of/destroyed keeping in view —
a: Rules relating to official secrets as well as financial prudence
e: Rule 218(iv): "to ensure compliance with rules relating to official secrets as well as financial prudence".
